claims.text: The baseline FeCoNi alloy is single-phase fcc.
The baseline FeCoNi alloy has high saturation magnetization.
The baseline alloy has a coercivity of approximately 100 Oe.
The proposed intervention is addition of 4 at.% Al followed by heat treatment at 750°C for 45 minutes and controlled slow cooling.
The specified Al addition and thermal treatment will nucleate fine Al-rich secondary precipitates.
The Al-rich precipitates will be finely dispersed within the fcc matrix.
The Al-rich precipitates will introduce additional magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
The Al-rich precipitates will act as pinning sites for magnetic domain walls.
Additional anisotropy and domain-wall pinning will increase coercivity.
The intervention will not substantially compromise the high saturation magnetization of the fcc matrix.
The modified alloy will have coercivity above 125 Oe, representing more than a 25% increase from an approximately 100 Oe baseline.
The treatment can retain a primary fcc matrix while permitting secondary precipitate formation.
Minor processing differences may change the volume fraction and distribution of Al-rich precipitates and therefore the magnitude of coercivity enhancement.
Preserving high saturation magnetization while increasing coercivity requires optimization.

contradictions.description: The composition is said to remain within the FeCoNi system, but adding 4 at.% Al makes the modified material a quaternary Fe-Co-Ni-Al alloy rather than a strictly ternary FeCoNi alloy.
